source: Rizwin's companion guide "Prophetic Duas, Sahabi Narratives, Hadith Proofs & Surah Headings" (uploaded 2026-11-12), Part 1. Text kept as given.

m1.heading: The Nightly Angelic Guard: Unbroken Protection From Satan Until Dawn
m1.story: The Prophet ﷺ entrusted **Abu Hurairah (رضي الله عنه)** to guard the dates of Zakat (Ramadan charity). For three consecutive nights, a disguised intruder sneaked in to steal handfuls of food, pleading poverty and dependents each time Abu Hurairah caught him. On the third night, to avoid being taken to the Prophet ﷺ, the prisoner taught Abu Hurairah to recite *Ayat al-Kursi* at bedtime—which the Prophet ﷺ confirmed the next morning was the truth spoken by Satan himself ([Sahih al-Bukhari 2311](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2311)). Additionally, in [Hisn al-Muslim 71](https://sunnah.com/hisn:71), the Prophet ﷺ taught the Companions to recite it after every obligatory prayer.
m1.narrative: Narrated Abu Huraira: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) deputed me to keep Sadaqat (al-Fitr) of Ramadan. A comer came and started taking handfuls of the foodstuff (of the Sadaqa) stealthily. I took hold of him and said, "By Allah, I will take you to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)." He said, "I am needy and have many dependents, and I am in great need." I released him, and in the morning Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) asked me, "What did your prisoner do yesterday?" I said, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! The person complained of being needy and of having many dependents, so, I pitied him and let him go." Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "Indeed, he told you a lie and he will be coming again." I believed that he would show up again as Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) had told me that he would return. So, I waited for him watchfully. When he (showed up and) started stealing handfuls of foodstuff, I caught hold of him again and said, "I will definitely take you to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ). He said, "Leave me, for I am very needy and have many dependents. I promise I will not come back again." I pitied him and let him go. In the morning Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) asked me, "What did your prisoner do." I replied, "O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! He complained of his great need and of too many dependents, so I took pity on him and set him free." Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "Verily, he told you a lie and he will return." I waited for him attentively for the third time, and when he (came and) started stealing handfuls of the foodstuff, I caught hold of him and said, "I will surely take you to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as it is the third time you promise not to return, yet you break your promise and come." He said, "(Forgive me and) I will teach you some words with which Allah will benefit you." I asked, "What are they?" He replied, "Whenever you go to bed, recite Ayat-al-Kursi from the beginning to the end — 'Allahu la ilaha illa huwa-l-Haiy-ul-Qaiyum' — (If you do so), Allah will appoint a guard for you who will stay with you and no satan will come near you till morning." So, I released him. In the morning, Allah's Apostle asked, "What did your prisoner do yesterday?" I replied, "He claimed that he would teach me some words by which Allah will benefit me, so I let him go." Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) asked, "What are they?" I replied, "He said to me, 'Whenever you go to bed, recite Ayat-al-Kursi from the beginning to the end — Allahu la ilaha illa huwa-lHaiy-ul-Qaiyum —.' He further said to me, '(If you do so), Allah will appoint a guard for you who will stay with you, and no satan will come near you till morning.'" (Abu Huraira or another sub-narrator) added that they (the companions) were very keen to do good deeds. The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "He really spoke the truth, although he is an absolute liar. Do you know whom you were talking to, these three nights, O Abu Huraira?" Abu Huraira said, "No." He said, "It was Satan." — [Sahih al-Bukhari 2311](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2311)
benefits: **Bedtime Recitation:** Allah appoints a dedicated guardian angel over the reciter all night, and no devil (Shaytan) can approach them until morning ([Sahih al-Bukhari 2311](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2311)).
**Morning & Evening Recitation:** Protection from the harm of jinn from morning until evening, and from evening until morning ([Hisn al-Muslim 75](https://sunnah.com/hisn:75)).
**After Every Obligatory Prayer:** Nothing stands between the reciter and entering Paradise except death ([Hisn al-Muslim 71](https://sunnah.com/hisn:71)).

m2.heading: The Threefold Shield: Complete Sufficiency Against Every Fear, Illness & Evil
m2.story: On a pitch-black, stormy, rainy night, **'Abdullah ibn Khubayb (رضي الله عنه)** and his companions went out searching for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to lead them in prayer. Seeing them out in the fearful dark and rain, the Prophet ﷺ repeatedly prompted 'Abdullah ibn Khubayb: *"Say!"* When 'Abdullah asked what he should say, the Prophet ﷺ taught him to recite *Surah Al-Ikhlas* and *Al-Mu'awwidhatayn* (*Surah Al-Falaq* and *Surah An-Nas*) three times every morning and evening ([Sunan Abi Dawud 5082](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5082)). Furthermore, **'Aishah (رضي الله عنها)** narrated how the Prophet ﷺ cupped his hands, blew these three Surahs into them, and wiped over his body every night and during his final illness ([Sahih al-Bukhari 5017](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5017)).
m2.narrative:
Narrated Abdullah ibn Khubayb: We went out one rainy and intensely dark night to look for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to lead us in prayer, and when we found him, he asked: Have you prayed?, but I did not say anything. So he said: Say, but I did not say anything. He again said: Say, but I did not say anything. He then said: Say. So I said: What am I to say? He said: Say: "Say, He is Allah, One," and al-Mu'awwadhatan three times in the morning and evening; they will serve you for every purpose. — [Sunan Abi Dawud 5082](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5082)

Narrated 'Aisha: Whenever the Prophet (ﷺ) went to bed every night, he used to cup his hands together and blow over it after reciting Surat Al-Ikhlas, Surat Al-Falaq and Surat An-Nas, and then rub his hands over whatever parts of his body he was able to rub, starting with his head, face and front of his body. He used to do that three times. — [Sahih al-Bukhari 5017](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5017)
benefits: **Complete Sufficiency:** Reciting them 3 times in the morning and evening suffices and protects a believer against every harm, anxiety, envy, magic, and unseen evil ([Sunan Abi Dawud 5082](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5082)).

**Physical & Spiritual Protection at Sleep:** Cupping the hands, blowing into them with these three Surahs, and wiping over the body shields the believer through the night ([Sahih al-Bukhari 5017](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5017)).

m3.heading: Entering the Day Under Allah's Sovereignty: Relief from Laziness, Arrogance & the Grave
m3.story: **'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (رضي الله عنه)** closely observed and transmitted the exact words the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would supplicate when entering the morning and evening to anchor the heart in Allah's dominion and seek protection from internal weakness (sloth and arrogance) and afterlife punishment ([Sahih Muslim 2723a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2723a)).
m3.narrative: Abdullah b. Mas'ud reported that when it was evening Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) used to supplicate: "We entered upon evening and the whole Kingdom of Allah also entered upon evening and praise is due to Allah. There is no god but Allah, the One Who has no partner with Him." Hasan said that Zubaid reported to him that he memorised it from Ibrahim in these very words: "His is the Sovereignty and Praise is due to Him, and He is Potent over everything. O Allah, I beg of Thee the good of this night and I seek refuge in Thee from the evil of this night and the evil which follows it. O Allah, I seek refuge in Thee from sloth, from the evil of vanity. O Allah, I seek refuge in Thee from torment in the Hell-Fire and from torment in the grave." — [Sahih Muslim 2723a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2723a)
benefits: **Securing Daily Goodness:** Asks Allah for the best of the new day or night and shields against the evil within it and what follows it ([Sahih Muslim 2723a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2723a)).

**Deliverance from Sloth & Arrogance:** Protects the believer from laziness (*al-kasal*), the evil of vanity/senility (*su' al-kibar*), and the torment of the Fire and the grave ([Sahih Muslim 2723a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2723a)).

m4.heading: The Antidote to Worldly & Spiritual Grief: Entrusting Every Burden to the Lord of the Mighty Throne
m4.story: Revealed to console the Prophet ﷺ when people turned away ([Surah At-Tawbah 9:129](https://quran.com/at-tawbah/129)), the Companion **Abu ad-Darda' (رضي الله عنه)** taught that whoever repeats these words seven times in the morning and evening will have Allah suffice them against whatever causes them grief or anxiety ([Sunan Abi Dawud 5081](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5081); [Hisn al-Muslim 83](https://sunnah.com/hisn:83)).
m4.narrative: Abu al-Darda' said: If anyone says seven times morning and evening: "Allah sufficeth me: there is no god but He; on him is my trust — He, the Lord of the Throne (of glory) Supreme", Allah will be sufficient for him against anything which grieves him, whether he is true or false in (repeating) them. — [Sunan Abi Dawud 5081](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5081)
benefits: **Removal of Every Worry:** Allah suffices the reciter against all worldly and hereafter matters that cause grief, anxiety, or distress when recited 7 times morning and evening ([Sunan Abi Dawud 5081](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5081); [Hisn al-Muslim 83](https://sunnah.com/hisn:83)).

m5.heading: Renewing the Covenant of Faith: Starting Every Day on the Pure Fitrah of Islam
m5.story: **'Abdur-Rahman ibn Abza (رضي الله عنه)** and **Ubayy ibn Ka'b (رضي الله عنه)** reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to teach his Companions to say this declaration every morning and evening so that they renew their pledge to die and live upon pure *Fitrah* (natural monotheism), the word of sincerity (*Kalimat al-Ikhlas*), the religion of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and the upright way of Prophet Ibrahim (عليه السلام) ([Hisn al-Muslim 90](https://sunnah.com/hisn:90)).
m5.narrative: Aṣbahnā `alā fiṭrati 'l-Islām, wa `alā kalimati 'l-ikhlās, wa `alā dīni nabiyyinā Muḥammadin (ṣallallāhu `alayhi wa sallam), wa `alā millati abīnā Ibrāhīm, ḥanīfan Musliman wa mā kāna mina 'l-mushrikīn. ("We have entered a new day upon the natural religion of Islam, the word of sincere devotion, the religion of our Prophet Muhammad (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), and the faith of our father Ibrahim. He was upright (in worshipping Allah), and a Muslim. He was not of those who worship others besides Allah.") — Reported by 'Abdur-Rahman ibn Abza in Musnad Ahmad and An-Nasa'i ([Hisn al-Muslim 90](https://sunnah.com/hisn:90))
benefits: **Firmness on Tawhid:** Anchors the believer's heart at dawn and dusk upon pure monotheism, shielding against shirk (associating partners with Allah) and spiritual deviation ([Hisn al-Muslim 90](https://sunnah.com/hisn:90)).

m6.heading: The Six-Direction Shield: Total Well-Being in Faith, Family, Wealth & Protection From Sudden Calamity
m6.story: **'Abdullah ibn 'Umar (رضي الله عنهما)** testified that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ *never* left off reciting these comprehensive words every single morning and evening—asking Allah for pardon, concealing of faults, calming of fears, and protection from all six directions (front, back, right, left, above, and beneath) ([Sunan Abi Dawud 5074](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5074)).
m6.narrative: Narrated Abdullah ibn Umar: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) never failed to utter these supplications in the evening and in the morning: "O Allah, I ask Thee for security in this world and in the Hereafter: O Allah! I ask Thee for forgiveness and security in my religion and my worldly affairs, in my family and my property; O Allah! conceal my fault or faults (according to Uthman's version), and keep me safe from the things which I fear; O Allah! guard me in front of me and behind me, on my right hand and on my left, and from above me: and I seek in Thy greatness from receiving unexpected harm from below me." Abu Dawud said: Waki' said: That is to say, swallowing by the earth. — [Sunan Abi Dawud 5074](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5074)
benefits: **Protection Across All Life Domains:** Secures divine pardon (*'afw*) and safety (*'afiyah*) in one's religion, worldly life, family, and wealth ([Sunan Abi Dawud 5074](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5074)).
**Concealing Faults & Calming Fear:** Replaces anxiety and fear with divine security and conceals personal shortcomings ([Sunan Abi Dawud 5074](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5074)).
**360-Degree Physical & Spiritual Guard:** Protects from harm coming from all six directions, including sudden catastrophe from beneath ([Sunan Abi Dawud 5074](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5074)).

m7.heading: Calling the Angels & Throne-Bearers to Witness: Complete Emancipation From the Fire
m7.story: **Anas ibn Malik (رضي الله عنه)**, who served the Prophet ﷺ for ten years in Madinah, narrated this promise of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: whoever calls Allah, the bearers of His Throne, His angels, and all creation to witness Allah's Oneness and Muhammad's Prophethood four times in the morning or evening is freed completely from the Hellfire ([Sunan Abi Dawud 5069](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5069)).
m7.narrative: Narrated Anas ibn Malik: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: If anyone says in the morning or in the evening: "O Allah! in the morning we call Thee, the bearers of Thy Throne, Thy angels and all Thy creatures to witness that thou art Allah (God) than Whom alone there is no god, and that Muhammad is Thy Servant and Apostle," Allah will emancipate his fourth from Hell; if anyone says twice, Allah will emancipate his half; if anyone says it thrice, Allah will emancipate three-fourth; and if he says four times, Allah will emancipate him from Hell. — [Sunan Abi Dawud 5069](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5069)
benefits: **Progressive Liberation from Hell:** Saying it 1 time frees a quarter of the person from Hell; 2 times frees half; 3 times frees three-quarters; and 4 times secures full emancipation from the Fire ([Sunan Abi Dawud 5069](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5069)). (Note: Graded *Hasan* by Ibn Baz and Ibn Hajar; graded *Da'if* by Al-Albani, as noted on the site).

m8.heading: Entrusting Every Breath to Allah: Mindful Transition Through Dawn, Dusk, Life & Resurrection
m8.story: **Abu Hurairah (رضي الله عنه)** taught the Companions how the Prophet ﷺ greeted every sunrise and sunset by acknowledging that we only wake, enter evening, live, die, and rise again through Allah's power ([Sunan Abi Dawud 5068](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5068)).
m8.narrative: Narrated AbuHurayrah: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to say in the morning: "O Allah, by Thee we come to the morning, by Thee we come to the evening, by Thee are we resurrected." In the evening he would say: "O Allah, by Thee we come to the evening, by Thee we die, and to Thee are we resurrected." — [Sunan Abi Dawud 5068](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5068)
benefits: **Constant Reliance on Allah:** Connects daily waking and sleeping to the ultimate reality of life, death, and resurrection before Allah ([Sunan Abi Dawud 5068](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5068)).

m9.heading: The Key to Complete Gratitude: Fulfilling Thanks for Every Blessing of the Day & Night
m9.story: The Companion **'Abdullah ibn Ghannam al-Bayadi (رضي الله عنه)** narrated that the Prophet ﷺ taught the believers a concise declaration that fulfills the obligation of thanking Allah (*Shukr*) for every blessing experienced during that day or night ([Sunan Abi Dawud 5073](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5073)).
m9.narrative: Narrated Abdullah ibn Ghannam: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: If anyone says in the morning: "O Allah! whatever favour has come to me, it comes from Thee alone Who has no partner; to Thee praise is due and thanksgiving," he will have expressed full thanksgiving for the day; and if anyone says the same in the evening, he will have expressed full thanksgiving for the night. — [Sunan Abi Dawud 5073](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5073)
benefits: **Complete Daily & Nightly Shukr:** Saying it in the morning discharges one's thanksgiving for the entire day, and saying it in the evening discharges one's thanksgiving for the entire night ([Sunan Abi Dawud 5073](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5073)).

m10.heading: The Shield of Physical Vitality: Preserving Health, Hearing & Sight While Warding Off Poverty
m10.story: When **'Abdur-Rahman ibn Abi Bakrah** heard his father, the noble Companion **Abu Bakrah Nufay' ibn al-Harith (رضي الله عنه)**, repeating this supplication three times every morning and three times every evening, he asked him why he never missed it. Abu Bakrah explained that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ supplicating with these exact words for bodily health, hearing, sight, and refuge from disbelief, poverty, and the torment of the grave ([Sunan Abi Dawud 5090](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5090)).
m10.narrative: Narrated AbuBakrah: AbdurRahman ibn AbuBakrah said that he told his father: O my father! I hear you supplicating every morning: "O Allah! Grant me health in my body. O Allah! Grant me good hearing. O Allah! Grant me good eyesight. There is no god but Thou." You repeat them three times in the morning and three times in the evening. He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) using these words as a supplication and I like to follow his practice. The transmitter, Abbas, said in this version: And you say: "O Allah! I seek refuge in Thee from infidelity and poverty. O Allah! I seek refuge in Thee from punishment in the grave. There is no god but Thee". You repeat them three times in the morning and three times in the evening, and use them as a supplication. I like to follow his practice. — [Sunan Abi Dawud 5090](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5090)
benefits: **Preservation of Physical Faculties:** Protects one's bodily vigor, hearing, and eyesight throughout life ([Sunan Abi Dawud 5090](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5090)).

**Protection from Poverty, Disbelief & Grave Torment:** Pairs physical well-being with protection against destitution (*al-faqr*), disbelief (*al-kufr*), and the punishment of the grave ([Sunan Abi Dawud 5090](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5090)).

m11.heading: The Master Plea for Forgiveness: Guaranteed Entry into Paradise for Day & Night
m11.story: The Prophet ﷺ taught **Shaddad ibn Aws (رضي الله عنه)** the single noblest formula for seeking Allah's forgiveness (*Sayyid al-Istighfar*), combining humble confession of one's sins with gratitude for Allah's blessings, and attached to it a direct promise of Paradise ([Sahih al-Bukhari 6306](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6306)).
m11.narrative: Narrated Shaddad bin Aus: The Prophet (ﷺ) said "The most superior way of asking for forgiveness from Allah is: 'O Allah, You are my Lord, there is none worthy of worship except You. You have created me, and I am Your servant, and I am faithful to Your covenant and promise as much as I can. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge Your blessings upon me, and I admit my sins. So forgive me, for none forgives sins except You.' The Prophet (ﷺ) added: 'If somebody recites it during the day with firm faith in it, and dies on the same day before the evening, he will be from the people of Paradise; and if somebody recites it at night with firm faith in it, and dies before the morning, he will be from the people of Paradise.'" — [Sahih al-Bukhari 6306](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6306)
benefits: **Guaranteed Paradise Upon Death:** Whoever recites it with conviction in the morning and passes away before evening enters Paradise; whoever recites it with conviction at night and passes away before morning enters Paradise ([Sahih al-Bukhari 6306](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6306)).
**Complete Forgiveness of Sins:** Recognized by the Prophet ﷺ as the highest and most complete form of *Istighfar* ([Sahih al-Bukhari 6306](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6306)).

m12.heading: The Shield Taught to Abu Bakr as-Siddiq: Protection From the Evil of One's Own Soul & Satan's Traps
m12.story: **Abu Bakr as-Siddiq (رضي الله عنه)** came directly to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked: *"O Messenger of Allah! Command me with words to say in the morning and in the evening."* The Prophet ﷺ taught him this powerful refuge from the unseen traps of the ego (*nafs*) and the devil ([Sunan Abi Dawud 5067](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5067)).
m12.narrative: Narrated AbuHurayrah: AbuBakr as-Siddiq said: Messenger of Allah! command me something to say in the morning and in the evening. He said: Say "O Allah, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Who knowest the unseen and the seen, Lord and Possessor of everything. I testify that there is no god but Thee; I seek refuge in Thee from the evil within myself, from the evil of the devil, and his (incitement to) attributing partners (to Allah)." He said: Say this in the morning, and in the evening, and when you go to bed. — [Sunan Abi Dawud 5067](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5067)
benefits: **Protection from Internal & External Harm:** Guards the believer in the morning, evening, and at bedtime from the evil of one's own soul, the plots of Shaytan, and falling into shirk or harming another Muslim ([Sunan Abi Dawud 5067](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5067)).

m13.heading: The Promise of Divine Satisfaction: How to Make It Incumbent Upon Allah to Please You
m13.story: In the mosque of Hims, **Abu Sallam** saw a venerable Companion who had personally served the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (**Thawban (رضي الله عنه)**) and asked him for a hadith he heard directly from the Prophet's ﷺ lips with no intermediary between them. The Companion shared this direct promise of how a believer earns Allah's guaranteed pleasure ([Sunan Abi Dawud 5072](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5072)).
m13.narrative: Narrated A man: AbuSallam told that he was in the mosque of Hims. A man passed him and the people said about him that he served the Prophet (ﷺ). He (AbuSallam) went to him and said: Tell me any tradition which you heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and there were no man between him and you. He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: If anyone says in the morning and in the evening: "I am pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, with Muhammad as Prophet," Allah will certainly please him. — [Sunan Abi Dawud 5072](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5072)
benefits: **Allah's Guaranteed Pleasure:** It becomes a promised right upon Allah to make the reciter pleased and satisfied on the Day of Resurrection ([Sunan Abi Dawud 5072](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5072)).

m14.heading: The Shield Against Sudden Calamity: Protection From Every Harm on Earth and in Heaven
m14.story: Narrated by **'Uthman ibn 'Affan (رضي الله عنه)** via his son **Aban ibn 'Uthman**. Later in life, when Aban suffered partial paralysis (hemiplegia) and a student looked at him in surprise because he was the narrator of this hadith, Aban swore by Allah that neither he nor 'Uthman lied about the Prophet ﷺ, explaining: *"That day when I was afflicted by it, I had become angry and forgot to say them!"* ([Sunan Abi Dawud 5088](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5088)).
m14.narrative: Narrated Uthman ibn Affan: Aban ibn Uthman said: I heard Uthman ibn Affan (his father) say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: If anyone says three times: "In the name of Allah, when Whose name is mentioned nothing on Earth or in Heaven can cause harm, and He is the Hearer, the Knower" he will not suffer sudden affliction till the morning, and if anyone says this in the morning, he will not suffer sudden affliction till the evening. Aban was afflicted by some paralysis and when a man who heard the tradition began to look at him, he said to him: Why are you looking at me? I swear by Allah, I did not tell a lie about Uthman, nor did Uthman tell a lie about the Prophet (ﷺ), but that day when I was afflicted by it, I became angry and forgot to say them. — [Sunan Abi Dawud 5088](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5088)
benefits: **Immunity from Sudden Calamity:** Reciting it 3 times in the evening protects from sudden affliction until morning, and reciting it 3 times in the morning protects from sudden affliction until evening ([Sunan Abi Dawud 5088](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5088)).
**Protection from All Harm:** Nothing on earth or in the heavens can harm the reciter ([Sunan Abi Dawud 5088](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5088)).

m15.heading: The Fivefold Daily Reward: 100 Sins Erased, 100 Good Deeds Written & An All-Day Fortress Against Satan
m15.story: Taught by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and transmitted by **Abu Hurairah (رضي الله عنه)** as the supreme daily remembrance that no one on earth can surpass in reward on that day except one who recites even more ([Sahih al-Bukhari 3293](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3293)).
m15.narrative: Narrated Abu Huraira: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "If one says one-hundred times in one day: 'None has the right to be worshipped but Allah, the Alone Who has no partners, to Him belongs Dominion and to Him belong all the Praises, and He has power over all things (i.e. Omnipotent)', one will get the reward of manumitting ten slaves, and one-hundred good deeds will be written in his account, and one-hundred bad deeds will be wiped off or erased from his account, and on that day he will be protected from the morning till evening from Satan, and nobody will be superior to him except one who has done more than that which he has done." — [Sahih al-Bukhari 3293](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3293)
benefits: **Reward of Freeing 10 Slaves:** Grants the immense reward of emancipating ten souls ([Sahih al-Bukhari 3293](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3293)).
**100 Good Deeds & 100 Sins Erased:** Writes 100 good deeds and wipes away 100 sins ([Sahih al-Bukhari 3293](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3293)).
**All-Day Fortress Against Satan:** Serves as a protective shield (*hirz*) from Shaytan from morning until evening ([Sahih al-Bukhari 3293](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3293)).

m16.heading: Tenfold Mercy From Allah: How Sending Blessings Upon the Prophet ﷺ Suffices Every Worry
m16.story: Narrated by **Abu Hurairah (رضي الله عنه)** that the Prophet ﷺ promised ten blessings from Allah for every single blessing sent upon him ([Sahih Muslim 408](https://sunnah.com/muslim:408)). Furthermore, when the Companion **Ubayy ibn Ka'b (رضي الله عنه)** asked the Prophet ﷺ what would happen if he dedicated his entire supplication time to sending Salawat upon him, the Prophet ﷺ replied: *"Then your worries will be sufficed and your sins will be forgiven"* ([Jami' at-Tirmidhi 2457](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:2457)).
m16.narrative: Abu Huraira reported: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "He who blesses me once, Allah would bless him ten times." — [Sahih Muslim 408](https://sunnah.com/muslim:408)
benefits: **Tenfold Divine Mercy:** For every single Salawat recited, Allah sends ten blessings of mercy and honor upon the servant ([Sahih Muslim 408](https://sunnah.com/muslim:408)).

m17.heading: The Dawn Blueprint for a Blessed Day: Beneficial Knowledge, Pure Provision & Accepted Deeds
m17.story: The Mother of the Believers, **Umm Salamah (رضي الله عنها)**, observed that every morning immediately after giving the *Salam* of the Fajr prayer, the Prophet ﷺ would ask Allah for the three pillars of a successful day: beneficial knowledge, lawful provision, and accepted deeds ([Sunan Ibn Majah 925](https://sunnah.com/ibnmajah:925)).
m17.narrative: It was narrated from Umm Salamah that when the Prophet (ﷺ) performed the Subh (morning prayer), while he said the Salam, he would say: "Allahumma inni as'aluka 'ilman nafi'an, wa rizqan tayyiban, wa 'amalan mutaqabbalan (O Allah, I ask You for beneficial knowledge, goodly provision and acceptable deeds)." — [Sunan Ibn Majah 925](https://sunnah.com/ibnmajah:925)
benefits: **Aligns the Entire Day:** Sets the believer's morning intention upon knowledge that benefits, halal sustenance (*rizq tayyib*), and righteous actions accepted by Allah ([Sunan Ibn Majah 925](https://sunnah.com/ibnmajah:925)).

m18.heading: The Lifeline in Times of Distress: Calling Upon the Ever-Living Sustainer to Set All Affairs Right
m18.story: **Anas ibn Malik (رضي الله عنه)** reported that whenever any heavy matter distressed or grieved the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he would cry out to Allah using His Greatest Names (*Al-Hayy Al-Qayyum*) ([Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3524](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3524)). Likewise, **Abu Bakrah (رضي الله عنه)** transmitted the Prophet's ﷺ teaching that the supplication of one in distress is to ask Allah not to leave them to themselves for even the blink of an eye ([Sunan Abi Dawud 5090](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5090)).
m18.narrative:
Anas bin Malik said: "Whenever a matter would distress him, the Prophet (ﷺ) would say: 'O Living, O Self-Sustaining Sustainer! In Your Mercy do I seek relief (Yā Ḥayyu yā Qayyūm, bi-raḥmatika astaghīth).'" — [Jami` at-Tirmidhi 3524](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3524)

Narrated AbuBakrah: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The supplications to be used by one who is distressed are: 'O Allah! Thy mercy is what I hope for. Do not abandon me to myself for an instant, but put all my affairs in good order for me. There is no god but Thou.'" — [Sunan Abi Dawud 5090](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5090)
benefits: **Immediate Relief in Crisis:** Invokes Allah by His Greatest Names (*Al-Hayy Al-Qayyum*) to rectify all personal and worldly affairs and prevent self-reliance for even the blink of an eye ([Jami` at-Tirmidhi 3524](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3524); [Sunan Abi Dawud 5090](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5090)).

m19.heading: Outweighing Hours of Worship: The Four Phrases the Prophet ﷺ Taught Juwayriyah (رضي الله عنها)
m19.story: One morning, the Prophet ﷺ left the apartment of his wife, the Mother of the Believers **Juwayriyah bint al-Harith (رضي الله عنها)**, at Fajr while she sat in her prayer place making dhikr. When he returned in the late forenoon (*Duha*), she was still sitting in the exact same spot. Seeing her hours of tireless effort, he gently taught her four phrases that, when said three times, outweigh all the remembrance she had done from dawn until forenoon ([Sahih Muslim 2726a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2726a)).
m19.narrative: Juwairiya reported that Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) came out from (her apartment) in the morning as she was busy in observing her dawn prayer in her place of worship. He came back in the forenoon and she was still sitting there. He (the Holy Prophet) said to her: "You have been in the same seat since I left you." She said: "Yes." Thereupon Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) said: "I recited four words three times after I left you and if these are to be weighed against what you have recited since morning these would outweigh them and (these words) are: 'Hallowed be Allah and praise is due to Him according to the number of His creation and according to the pleasure of His Self and according to the weight of His Throne and according to the ink (used in recording) words (for His Praise).'" — [Sahih Muslim 2726a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2726a)
benefits: **Multiplied Scale of Reward:** Saying these four phrases 3 times in the morning outweighs hours of continuous individual dhikr from dawn until late morning ([Sahih Muslim 2726a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2726a)).

m20.heading: Protection From Poisonous Stings & Unseen Harm: The Refuge Taught After a Scorpion Sting
m20.story: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ complaining of the severe pain he suffered all night after being stung by a scorpion. The Prophet ﷺ told him that had he recited this refuge when evening fell, the scorpion's sting would not have harmed him ([Sahih Muslim 2709b](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2709b); [Jami` at-Tirmidhi 3604b](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3604b)). Additionally, the female Companion **Khawlah bint Hakim as-Sulamiyyah (رضي الله عنها)** narrated that whoever stops at any destination or lodging and recites it will not be harmed by anything until they depart ([Sahih Muslim 2708a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2708a)).
m20.narrative:
Abu Hurairah narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever says three times when he reaches the evening: 'I seek refuge in Allah's Perfect Words from the evil of what He created (A`ūdhu bikalimātillāhit-tāmmāti min sharri mā khalaq),' no poisonous sting shall harm him that night." (One of the narrators) Suhail said: "So our family used to learn it and they used to say it every night. A girl among them was stung, and she did not feel any pain." — [Jami` at-Tirmidhi 3604b](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3604b)

Khaula bint Hakim Sulamiyya reported: I heard Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying: "When anyone lands at a place, and then says: 'I seek refuge in the Perfect Word of Allah from the evil of what He has created,' nothing would harm him until he marches from that stopping place." — [Sahih Muslim 2708a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2708a)
benefits: **Immunity from Venom & Nightly Harm:** Reciting it 3 times in the evening prevents scorpions, snakes, and noxious creatures from harming the reciter through the night ([Jami` at-Tirmidhi 3604b](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3604b)).

**Complete Safety in Any Lodging or Travel Stop:** Saying it upon arriving at any place guarantees nothing will harm the person until they leave that place ([Sahih Muslim 2708a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2708a)).

m21.heading: Polishing a Heavy Heart: Seeking Forgiveness 70 to 100 Times Daily
m21.story: Both **Abu Hurairah (رضي الله عنه)** and **Al-Agharr al-Muzani (رضي الله عنه)** narrated how the Prophet ﷺ urged the Companions to constantly turn to Allah in repentance whenever they felt spiritual heaviness or a "shade/cloud" (*ghayn*) over the heart, sharing that he himself sought Allah's forgiveness 70 to 100 times every single day ([Sahih al-Bukhari 6307](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6307); [Sahih Muslim 2702a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2702a)).
m21.narrative:
Narrated Abu Huraira: I heard Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) saying: "By Allah! I ask for forgiveness from Allah and turn to Him in repentance more than seventy times a day." — [Sahih al-Bukhari 6307](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6307)

Al-Agharr al-Muzani, who was one amongst the Companions (of the Holy Prophet) reported that Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: "There is (at times) some sort of shade upon my heart, and I seek forgiveness from Allah a hundred times a day." — [Sahih Muslim 2702a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2702a)
benefits: **Clears Spiritual Heaviness:** Removes the spiritual cloudiness (*ghayn*) and constriction of the heart ([Sahih Muslim 2702a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2702a)).

**Continual Renewal of Repentance:** Follows the daily Prophetic sunnah of seeking forgiveness 70 to 100 times a day ([Sahih al-Bukhari 6307](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6307); [Sahih Muslim 2702b](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2702b)).

m22.heading: Wiping Away an Ocean of Sins: The 100-Time Daily Tasbih
m22.story: **Abu Hurairah (رضي الله عنه)** reported the glad tidings given by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to his Companions that repeating these two simple words 100 times wipes away a lifetime of minor sins, even if they are as vast as the foam of the ocean ([Sahih al-Bukhari 6405](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6405)).
m22.narrative: Narrated Abu Huraira: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "Whoever says, 'Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi,' one hundred times a day, will be forgiven all his sins even if they were as much as the foam of the sea." — [Sahih al-Bukhari 6405](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6405)
benefits: **Erasure of Sins Like Sea Foam:** Saying it 100 times in a day obliterates one's sins even if they equal the foam of the sea ([Sahih al-Bukhari 6405](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6405)).

m23.heading: The Daily Pilgrimage of the Heart: Earning the Complete Reward of Hajj & 'Umrah After Fajr
m23.story: **Anas ibn Malik (رضي الله عنه)** narrated how the Prophet ﷺ encouraged his Companions who longed for the immense reward of pilgrimage by teaching them this post-Fajr practice, repeating the word *"Complete"* three times for emphasis ([Jami` at-Tirmidhi 586](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:586)).
m23.narrative: Anas bin Malik narrated that: the Messenger of Allah said: "Whoever prays Fajr in congregation, then sits remembering Allah until the sun has risen, then he prays two Rak'ah, then for him is the reward like that of a Hajj and Umrah." He said: "The Messenger of Allah said: 'Complete, complete, complete.'" — [Jami` at-Tirmidhi 586](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:586)
benefits: **Full Reward of Hajj and 'Umrah:** Grants the reward of a complete, complete, complete Hajj and 'Umrah ([Jami` at-Tirmidhi 586](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:586)).

m24.heading: Beloved to the Most Merciful: Two Effortless Phrases That Tip the Scales on Judgment Day
m24.story: **Abu Hurairah (رضي الله عنه)** narrated this beloved teaching — with which Imam al-Bukhari chose to seal his entire *Sahih al-Bukhari* — showing how even the weakest or busiest believer can fill their scale of deeds with two effortless phrases ([Sahih al-Bukhari 6406](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6406)).
m24.narrative: Narrated Abu Huraira: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "There are two expressions which are very easy for the tongue to say, but they are very heavy in the balance and are very dear to The Beneficent (Allah), and they are, 'Subhan Allah Al-`Azim' and 'Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi.'" — [Sahih al-Bukhari 6406](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6406)
benefits: **Heavy on the Balance (*Mizan*):** Though effortless to pronounce, they weigh heavily on the Scale of Deeds on the Day of Judgment and are deeply beloved to Ar-Rahman ([Sahih al-Bukhari 6406](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6406)).

m25.heading: The Treasure From Beneath the Throne: Two Nightly Verses That Suffice You Against Everything
m25.story: **Abu Mas'ud al-Ansari al-Badri (رضي الله عنه)** narrated this while circumambulating the Ka'bah ([Sahih al-Bukhari 5009](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5009); [Sahih Muslim 808a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:808a)). Furthermore, **Ibn 'Abbas (رضي الله عنهما)** narrated that while Angel Jibril was sitting with the Prophet ﷺ, a gate in heaven opened that had never opened before, and an angel descended to give the Prophet ﷺ glad tidings of two lights never given to any prophet before him: *Surah Al-Fatihah* and the concluding verses of *Surah Al-Baqarah* ([Sahih Muslim 806](https://sunnah.com/muslim:806)).
m25.narrative:
Narrated Abu Mas'ud: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "If somebody recited the last two Verses of Surat Al-Baqara at night, that will be sufficient for him." — [Sahih al-Bukhari 5009](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5009)

Ibn 'Abbas reported that while Gabriel was sitting with the Apostle (ﷺ) he heard a creaking sound above him. He lifted his head and said: "This is a gate opened in heaven today which had never been opened before." Then when an angel descended through it, he said: "This is an angel who came down to the earth who had never come down before." He greeted and said: "Rejoice in two lights given to you which have not been given to any prophet before you: Fatihat al-Kitab and the concluding verses of Surah al-Baqara. You will never recite a letter from them for which you will not be given (a reward)." — [Sahih Muslim 806](https://sunnah.com/muslim:806)
benefits: **Complete Nightly Sufficiency:** Reciting verses 285–286 of Surah Al-Baqarah at night suffices the believer against all harm, anxiety, and evil that night ([Sahih al-Bukhari 5009](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5009); [Sahih Muslim 808a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:808a)).
**Guaranteed Answer to Every Word:** Every single letter recited from these verses is answered and rewarded by Allah ([Sahih Muslim 806](https://sunnah.com/muslim:806)).

m26.heading: A Treasure From the Vaults of Paradise: Surrendering Human Weakness for Allah's Infinite Strength
m26.story: During the march toward the Battle of Khaybar, as the army climbed over a high mountain pass, the soldiers raised their voices shouting *Takbir*. The Prophet ﷺ gently advised them to lower their voices because they were calling upon the All-Hearing Who was near to them. Meanwhile, **Abu Musa al-Ash'ari ('Abdullah ibn Qays, رضي الله عنه)** was walking right behind the Prophet's ﷺ mount, quietly repeating *La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah* under his breath. Hearing him, the Prophet ﷺ called out to him by name and revealed its status in Paradise ([Sahih al-Bukhari 4205](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4205)).
m26.narrative: Narrated Abu Musa Al-Ash`ari: When Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) fought the battle of Khaibar, or when Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) went towards it, (whenever) the people (passed over a high place overlooking a valley, they raised their voices saying, "Allahu-Akbar! Allahu-Akbar! None has the right to be worshipped except Allah." On that Allah's Apostle said (to them), "Lower your voices, for you are not calling a deaf or an absent one, but you are calling a Hearer Who is near and is with you." I was behind the riding animal of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and he heard me saying, "There is neither might, nor power but with Allah." On that he said to me, "O `Abdullah bin Qais!" I said, "Labbaik, O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)!" He said, "Shall I tell you a sentence which is one of the treasures of Paradise?" I said, "Yes, O Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)! Let my father and mother be sacrificed for your sake." He said, "It is: There is neither might nor power but with Allah (La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah)." — [Sahih al-Bukhari 4205](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4205)
benefits: **A Stored Treasure in Paradise:** Grants the reciter a precious treasure stored in the vaults of Jannah ([Sahih al-Bukhari 4205](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4205)).
**Strength in Hardship:** Helps a servant bear heavy burdens and overcome obstacles by relying on Allah's power rather than human strength ([Sahih al-Bukhari 4205](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4205)).

m27.heading: Better Than Everything the Sun Rises Upon: The Four Words Most Beloved to Allah
m27.story: **Abu Hurairah (رضي الله عنه)** narrated how the Prophet ﷺ shifted his Companions' perspective from worldly possessions to eternal wealth by declaring that uttering these four phrases is dearer to him than the entire world and everything the sun rises over ([Sahih Muslim 2695](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2695)).
m27.narrative: Abu Huraira reported Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying: "The uttering of (these words): 'Exalted is Allah (He is free from imperfection), all praise is due to Allah, there is no god but Allah, and Allah is the Greatest (SubhanAllah, wal-hamdulillah, wa la ilaha illallah, wallahu Akbar),' is dearer to me than anything over which the sun rises." — [Sahih Muslim 2695](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2695)
benefits: **Greater Than Worldly Riches:** More beloved and valuable in the sight of the Prophet ﷺ and in eternal reward than everything the sun shines upon ([Sahih Muslim 2695](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2695)).

m28.heading: Better Than a Household Servant: How the Prophet ﷺ Relieved Fatimah's Exhaustion & the Poor Companions' Grief
m28.story: This dua carries **two famous Sahabi relief stories** (including the exact incident of **Fatimah رضي الله عنها** you mentioned!):
m28.narrative:
Narrated `Ali: Fatima complained about the blisters on her hand because of using a mill-stone. She went to ask the Prophet for a servant, but she did not find him (at home) and had to inform `Aisha of her need. When he came, `Aisha informed him about it. `Ali added: The Prophet (ﷺ) came to us when we had gone to our beds. When I was going to get up, he said, "Stay in your places," and sat between us, till I felt the coolness of the feet on my chest. The Prophet (ﷺ) then said, "Shall I not tell you of a thing which is better for you than a servant? When you (both) go to your beds, say 'Allahu Akbar' thirty-three times, and 'Subhan Allah' thirty-three times, and 'Al-hamdu lillah' thirty-three times, for that is better for you than a servant." Ibn Seereen said, "'Subhan Allah' (is to be said for) thirty-four times." (And in the other narration: "recite Takbir thirty-four times, Tasbih thirty-three times, and Tahmid thirty-three times.") — [Sahih al-Bukhari 6318](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6318)

Abu Huraira reported Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying: "If anyone extols Allah after every prayer thirty-three times, and praises Allah thirty-three times, and declares His Greatness thirty-three times, ninety-nine times in all, and says to complete a hundred: 'There is no god but Allah, having no partner with Him, to Him belongs sovereignty and to Him is praise due, and He is Potent over everything,' his sins will be forgiven even if these are as abundant as the foam of the sea." — [Sahih Muslim 597a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:597a)
benefits: **Physical Strength & Relief from Exhaustion at Bedtime:** Grants bodily strength, removes the fatigue of hard labor and housework, and is better for the believer than having a domestic servant ([Sahih al-Bukhari 6318](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6318)).

**Forgiveness of Sins & Equalizing Charity Rewards After Prayer:** Erases sins even if they are as abundant as the foam of the ocean and allows those without wealth to catch up with the charity of the wealthy ([Sahih Muslim 597a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:597a)). ### Category 2: After and Within Prayer (3 Duas)

s1.heading: Purifying the Soul: Refuge From Unbeneficial Knowledge, an Unmoved Heart, an Insatiable Ego & Unanswered Dua
s1.story: When people asked the Companion **Zayd ibn Arqam (رضي الله عنه)** to teach them, he humbly declared: *"I am not going to say anything to you except the exact words that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say,"* and transmitted this comprehensive plea for soul-purification (*tazkiyah*) and refuge from four spiritual diseases ([Sahih Muslim 2722](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2722)).
s1.narrative: Zaid b. Arqam reported: I am not going to say anything but only that which Allah's Messenger (may peace be upon him) used to say. He used to supplicate: "O Allah, I seek refuge in Thee from incapacity, from sloth, from cowardice, from miserliness, decrepitude and from torment of the grave. O Allah, grant to my soul the sense of righteousness and purify it, for Thou art the Best Purifier thereof. Thou art the Protecting Friend thereof, and Guardian thereof. O Allah, I seek refuge in Thee from the knowledge which does not benefit, from the heart that does not entertain the fear (of Allah), from the soul that does not feel contented and the supplication that is not responded." — [Sahih Muslim 2722](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2722)
benefits: **Purification of the Soul (*Tazkiyat an-Nafs*):** Asks Allah directly to inspire the soul with *Taqwa* and purify it ([Sahih Muslim 2722](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2722)).

**Protection from Four Spiritual Spiritual Afflictions:** Shields against knowledge that brings no benefit, a hardened heart devoid of *khushu'*, an insatiable ego that is never satisfied, and having one's prayers go unanswered ([Sahih Muslim 2722](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2722)).

s2.heading: A Gift of Prophetic Love: The Post-Prayer Plea Taught Hand-in-Hand to Mu'adh ibn Jabal
s2.story: One day, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took the hand of his beloved Companion **Mu'adh ibn Jabal (رضي الله عنه)** and swore an oath of affection: *"By Allah, indeed I love you, O Mu'adh!"* Out of that deep love, he advised Mu'adh never to omit reciting this supplication at the end of every prayer. Mu'adh treasured it so deeply that he bequeathed it on his deathbed to his student As-Sunabihi, who bequeathed it to Abu 'Abdur-Rahman ([Sunan Abi Dawud 1522](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:1522)).
s2.narrative: Mu'adh b. Jabal reported that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) caught his hand and said: "By Allah, I love you, Mu'adh. I give some instruction to you. Never leave to recite this supplication after every (prescribed) prayer: 'O Allah, help me in remembering You, in giving You thanks, and worshipping You well (Allahumma a'inni 'ala dhikrika wa shukrika wa husni 'ibadatik).'" Mu'adh willed this supplication to the narrator al-Sunabihi and al-Sunabihi to Abu Abd al-Rahman. — [Sunan Abi Dawud 1522](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:1522)
benefits: **Divine Assistance in Worship:** Secures Allah's direct help (*tawfiq*) to keep the tongue moist with remembrance, the heart full of gratitude, and one's worship performed with excellence ([Sunan Abi Dawud 1522](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:1522)).

s3.heading: Gratitude That Shields for Life: Lifelong Protection From Any Trial or Illness You Witness
s3.story: **'Umar ibn al-Khattab (رضي الله عنه)** and **Abu Hurairah (رضي الله عنه)** narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught the believers what to whisper quietly in gratitude to Allah whenever they see someone suffering from a severe illness, physical trial, or tribulation ([Jami` at-Tirmidhi 3431](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3431)).
s3.narrative: Umar narrated that: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever sees a person afflicted and says: 'All praise is due to Allah Who saved me from that which He has afflicted you with, and blessed me greatly over many of those whom He has created (Al-ḥamdulillāhi alladhī `āfānī mimmabtalāka bihī wa faḍḍalanī `alā kathīrin mimman khalaqa tafḍīla),' then he shall be saved from that affliction for as long as he lives." — [Jami` at-Tirmidhi 3431](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3431)
benefits: **Lifelong Protection from That Trial:** Whoever says this quietly out of humble gratitude to Allah will never be struck by that specific illness or affliction for as long as they live ([Jami` at-Tirmidhi 3431](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3431)).

s4.heading: The Prophetic Touch of Healing: Calling Upon the True Healer to Leave No Trace of Illness
s4.story: **'Aishah (رضي الله عنها)** narrated that whenever anyone in the Prophet's ﷺ family fell ill, he would pass his right hand over the place of pain and recite this Ruqyah ([Sahih al-Bukhari 5735](https://sunnah.com/bukhari/76/50-65)). Later, when the scholar **Thabit al-Bunani** visited the Companion **Anas ibn Malik (رضي الله عنه)** and complained, *"O Abu Hamzah! I am sick,"* Anas immediately offered: *"Shall I treat you with the Ruqyah of Allah's Messenger ﷺ?"* and recited this exact supplication over him ([Sahih al-Bukhari 5742](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5742)).
s4.narrative: Narrated `Abdul `Aziz: Thabit and I went to Anas bin Malik. Thabit said, "O Abu Hamza! I am sick." On that Anas said, "Shall I treat you with the Ruqya of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)?" Thabit said, "Yes." Anas recited, "O Allah! The Lord of the people, the Remover of trouble! (Please) cure (Heal) (this patient), for You are the Healer. None brings about healing but You; a healing that will leave behind no ailment." — [Sahih al-Bukhari 5742](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5742)
benefits: **Complete Recovery Without Relapse:** Invokes Allah as *Ash-Shafi* (The Healer) to remove pain and grant a complete cure that leaves behind no lingering sickness ([Sahih al-Bukhari 5742](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5742)).

s5.heading: The Sevenfold Bedside Prayer: A Promised Cure When Visiting the Sick
s5.story: **'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas (رضي الله عنهما)** narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that whenever a Muslim visits a sick person whose decreed time of death has not yet arrived and recites this supplication in their presence seven times, Allah heals them of that sickness ([Sunan Abi Dawud 3106](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:3106)).
s5.narrative: Narrated Abdullah ibn Abbas: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "If anyone visits a sick whose time (of death) has not come, and says with him seven times: 'I ask Allah, the Mighty, the Lord of the mighty Throne, to cure you (As'alullahal-'Azim, Rabbal-'Arshil-'Azim, an yashfiyak),' Allah will cure him from that disease." — [Sunan Abi Dawud 3106](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:3106)
benefits: **Divine Healing for the Patient:** Provided the patient's appointed time of death has not arrived, Allah cures them from that illness when this dua is recited 7 times at their bedside ([Sunan Abi Dawud 3106](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:3106)).

s6.heading: When Worldly Trials Feel Heavy: The Prophet's ﷺ Parting Prayer for Certainty, Strength & Protection of Faith
s6.story: **'Abdullah ibn 'Umar (رضي الله عنهما)** noted that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ rarely stood up from any gathering without first making this deeply moving supplication *for his Companions*—asking Allah for fear of Him that blocks sin, certainty (*yaqin*) that makes worldly calamities feel light, preservation of hearing, sight, and strength into old age, and protection from making this world our greatest worry ([Jami` at-Tirmidhi 3502](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3502)).
s6.narrative: Ibn `Umar said: "Rarely would the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stand from a sitting until he supplicated with these words for his Companions: 'O Allah, apportion for us, fear of You, that shall come between us and disobedience of You, and of obedience to You, which shall cause us to obtain Your Paradise, and of certainty, which shall make the afflictions of the world easy for us, and enjoyment of our hearing, and our seeing, and our strength as long as You keep us alive, and make it the inheritor of us. And let our vengeance be upon those who have wronged us, and aid us against those who show enmity towards us, and do not make our affliction in our religion, and do not make this world our greatest concern, nor the limit of our knowledge, and do not give power over us to those who will not have mercy on us.'" — [Jami` at-Tirmidhi 3502](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3502)
benefits: **Makes Worldly Calamities Easy to Bear:** Grants deep certainty (*yaqin*) that lightens the pain of worldly trials ([Jami` at-Tirmidhi 3502](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3502)).

**Protects Religion, Senses & Priorities:** Preserves one's religion from trial, keeps the world from becoming one's biggest anxiety, maintains hearing, sight, and strength until death, and protects against merciless rulers or oppressors ([Jami` at-Tirmidhi 3502](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3502)).

s7.heading: Leaving Nothing Out: The All-Encompassing Supplication the Prophet ﷺ Taught 'Aishah (رضي الله عنها)
s7.story: One day, the Prophet ﷺ came to **'Aishah (رضي الله عنها)** while she was taking a long time praying and supplicating. He told her: *"O 'Aishah, you must adhere to the comprehensive, all-inclusive supplications (Al-Jawami' Al-Kawamil)!"* When she finished her prayer and asked him what those comprehensive words were, he taught her this masterpiece of a dua that asks for every good known and unknown, every prayer the Prophet ﷺ ever asked for, Paradise and what leads to it, and that every decree be turned into good ([Al-Adab Al-Mufrad 639](https://sunnah.com/adab:639); [Sunan Ibn Majah 3846](https://sunnah.com/ibnmajah:3846)).
s7.narrative: Umm Kulthum, the daughter of Abu Bakr, reported that 'A'isha said, "The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to me while I was praying when he needed something. I was taking a long time and he said, ''A'isha, you must make the comprehensive supplication.' When I finished, I asked, 'Messenger of Allah, what is the comprehensive supplication?' He said, 'Say: "O Allah, I ask You for all good, both sooner and later, what I know of it and what I do not know. I seek refuge with You from all evil, both sooner and later, what I know of it and what I do not know. I ask You for the Garden and whatever words or actions bring one near to it. I seek refuge with You from the Fire and whatever words or actions bring one near to it. I ask You by what Muhammad asked You and I seek refuge from You by what Muhammad sought refuge from and whatever fate You have decreed for me, make its end right guidance."'" — [Al-Adab Al-Mufrad 639](https://sunnah.com/adab:639) (See also [Sunan Ibn Majah 3846](https://sunnah.com/ibnmajah:3846))
benefits: **Includes Every Prophetic Dua at Once:** Automatically includes every good the Prophet ﷺ ever asked for and every protection he ever sought, covering both what the believer knows to ask for and what they do not even realize they need ([Al-Adab Al-Mufrad 639](https://sunnah.com/adab:639); [Sunan Ibn Majah 3846](https://sunnah.com/ibnmajah:3846)).

s8.heading: Shield Against Crushing Trials: Protection From Unbearable Calamity, Wretchedness & Gloating Enemies
s8.story: **Abu Hurairah (رضي الله عنه)** narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ constantly sought refuge from these four crushing hardships and commanded his Companions to seek refuge from them as well ([Sahih al-Bukhari 6347](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6347)).
s8.narrative: Narrated Abu Huraira: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) used to seek refuge with Allah from the difficult moment of a calamity and from being overtaken by destruction and from being destined to an evil end, and from the malicious joy of enemies. Sufyan said, "This narration contained three items only, but I added one. I do not know which one that was." — [Sahih al-Bukhari 6347](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6347)
benefits: **Protection from Four Overwhelming Hardships:** Guards against *jahd al-bala'* (exhaustive, unbearable trial), *darak ash-shaqa'* (being overtaken by misery/destruction), *su' al-qada'* (an evil decree/outcome), and *shamatat al-a'da'* (the malicious gloating of enemies when one is struck by hardship) ([Sahih al-Bukhari 6347](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6347)).

s9.heading: Paying Off a Mountain of Debt: The Prophetic Words 'Ali Taught a Struggling Man Seeking His Freedom
s9.story: A *Mukatab* (a contracted slave working to pay off his manumission price in installments) came to **'Ali ibn Abi Talib (رضي الله عنه)** in distress and said: *"Indeed, I am unable to pay off my contract of freedom, so help me!"* Rather than merely giving him a small sum, 'Ali taught him the exact words the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had taught him, promising that even if his debt was as huge as the mountain of *Sir* (a great mountain in Tayyi'), Allah would pay it off for him ([Jami` at-Tirmidhi 3563](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3563)).
s9.narrative: Ali [may Allah be pleased with him] narrated: that a Mukatib came to him and said: "Indeed I am not capable of my Kitabah so aid me." He said: "Should I not teach you words that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) taught me? If you had a debt upon you similar to the mountain of Sir, Allah would fulfill it for you. He said: 'Say: O Allah, suffice me with Your lawful against Your prohibited, and make me independent of all those besides You (Allāhummakfinī biḥalālika `an ḥarāmika, wa aghninī bi faḍlika `amman siwāka).'" — [Jami` at-Tirmidhi 3563](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3563)
benefits: **Repayment of Mountain-Sized Debts:** Allah opens doors to settle even overwhelming debts as large as a mountain ([Jami` at-Tirmidhi 3563](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3563)).

**Halal Sufficiency & Financial Dignity:** Suffices the believer with pure, lawful (*halal*) provision so they never need the unlawful (*haram*) or depend on anyone besides Allah ([Jami` at-Tirmidhi 3563](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3563)). ### Category 6: Family (3 Duas)

s10.heading: The Prophet's ﷺ Most Frequent Prayer: How This Verse Cured a Companion Wasting Away From Illness
s10.story: In addition to **Anas ibn Malik (رضي الله عنه)** reporting that this was the single most frequent supplication of the Prophet ﷺ ([Sahih Muslim 2690a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2690a); [Sahih al-Bukhari 6389](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6389)), Anas narrated an unforgettable healing story: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ visited a Muslim Companion who had become so wasted away by illness that he looked as frail and feeble as a baby bird (*farkh*). When the Prophet ﷺ asked him what he had been praying for, the sick man confessed he had been praying: *"O Allah, whatever punishment You are going to impose on me in the Hereafter, hasten it upon me in this world!"* The Prophet ﷺ exclaimed *SubhanAllah*, told him he could never bear Allah's punishment, and asked why he had not said *Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanatan wa fil-akhirati hasanatan wa qina 'adhaban-nar*. The Prophet ﷺ then made this exact dua for him, and Allah healed him on the spot ([Sahih Muslim 2688a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2688a)).
s10.narrative:
Anas reported that Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) visited a person from amongst the Muslims in order to inquire (about his health) who had grown feeble like the chicken. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: "Did you supplicate for anything or beg of Him about that?" He said: "Yes. I used to utter (these words): Impose punishment upon me earlier in this world, what Thou art going to impose upon me in the Hereafter." Thereupon Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: "Exalted is Allah (He is free from imperfection), you have neither the power nor forbearance to take upon yourself (the burden of His Punishment). Why did you not say this: O Allah, grant us good in the world and good in the Hereafter, and save us from the torment of Fire." He (the Prophet) made this supplication (for him) and he was all right. — [Sahih Muslim 2688a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2688a)

Qatada asked Anas which Supplication Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) frequently made. He said: "The supplication that he (the Prophet) made very frequently is this: 'O Allah, grant us the good in this world and the good in the Hereafter and save us from the torment of Hell-Fire.'" He (Qatada) said that whenever Anas had to supplicate he made this very supplication, and whenever he (intended) to make another supplication he (inserted) this very supplication in that. — [Sahih Muslim 2690a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2690a)
benefits: **Gathers All Worldly & Eternal Well-Being:** Encompasses health, halal provision, beneficial knowledge, a righteous spouse, Paradise in the Hereafter, and deliverance from the Fire ([Surah Al-Baqarah 2:201](https://quran.com/al-baqarah/201); [Sahih Muslim 2688a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2688a)).

s11.heading: Joy of the Eyes in Home & Hereafter: Raising a Righteous Family & Unbroken Sadaqah Jariyah
s11.story: In [Surah Al-Furqan 25:74](https://quran.com/al-furqan/74), Allah praises the *'Ibad ar-Rahman* (Servants of the Most Merciful) who pray for spouses and children who bring coolness and serenity to their eyes. Complementing this verse, **Abu Hurairah (رضي الله عنه)** narrated that the Prophet ﷺ taught that when a human being dies, all their deeds come to an end except three—one of which is a righteous child who continues to pray for them ([Sahih Muslim 1631](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1631)).
s11.narrative:
Quranic Verse: "˹They are˺ those who pray, 'Our Lord! Bless us with ˹pious˺ spouses and offspring who will be the joy of our hearts, and make us models for the righteous.'" — [Surah Al-Furqan 25:74](https://quran.com/al-furqan/74)

Abu Huraira (Allah be pleased with him) reported Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) as saying: "When a man dies, his acts come to an end, but three, recurring charity, or knowledge (by which people) benefit, or a pious child, who prays for him (for the deceased)." — [Sahih Muslim 1631](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1631)
benefits: **Marital & Family Peace (*Qurrat A'yun*):** Grants righteous spouses and children who bring deep spiritual joy and peace to the home ([Surah Al-Furqan 25:74](https://quran.com/al-furqan/74)).

**Unbroken Reward After Death:** A righteous child who supplicates for their parents continues to elevate their ranks in the grave after all other deeds have ceased ([Sahih Muslim 1631](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1631)).

s12.heading: Anchoring a Wavering Heart: Why the Prophet ﷺ Most Frequently Prayed "O Turner of the Hearts"
s12.story: Both **Anas ibn Malik (رضي الله عنه)** and the Mother of the Believers **Umm Salamah (رضي الله عنها)** asked the Prophet ﷺ about this dua. When **Anas** heard the Prophet ﷺ repeating *Ya Muqallibal-qulub, thabbit qalbi 'ala dinik*, Anas asked: *"O Prophet of Allah! We believe in you and what you have come with, so do you fear for us?"* ([Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2140](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:2140)). Similarly, when **Umm Salamah** was asked what supplication the Prophet ﷺ made most frequently in her home, she named this exact dua and explained that when she asked him why, he replied that every human heart lies between two Fingers of the Most Merciful ([Jami` at-Tirmidhi 3522](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3522); [Sahih Muslim 2655](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2655)).
s12.narrative:
Anas narrated: "The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.) would often say: Ya Muqallibal-qulub, thabbit qalbi 'ala dinik ('O Changer of the Hearts! Strengthen my heart upon Your Religion.') So I said: 'O Prophet of Allah! We believe in you and what you have come with, but do you fear for us?' He said: 'Yes. Indeed the hearts are between two Fingers of Allah's Fingers, He changes them as He wills.'" — [Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2140](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:2140)

Shahr bin Hawshab said: "I said to Umm Salamah: 'O Mother of the Believers! What was the supplication that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said most frequently when he was with you?' She said: 'The supplication he said most frequently was: "O Changer of the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion (Yā Muqallibal-qulūb, thabbit qalbī `alā dīnik)."' She said: 'So I said: "O Messenger of Allah, why do you supplicate so frequently: 'O Changer of the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion.' He said: 'O Umm Salamah! Verily, there is no human being except that his heart is between Two Fingers of the Fingers of Allah, so whomsoever He wills He makes steadfast, and whomever He wills He causes to deviate.'" — [Jami` at-Tirmidhi 3522](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3522)
benefits: **Firmness in Times of Doubt & Fitnah:** Keeps the believer's heart anchored upon Islam and obedience to Allah when trials and doubts cause hearts to waver ([Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2140](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:2140); [Sahih Muslim 2655](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2655)).

s13.heading: The Four Jewels of a Noble Life: Right Guidance, Piety, Moral Purity & Richness of the Soul
s13.story: **'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (رضي الله عنه)** narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ regularly supplicated with these four concise words that gather every spiritual and moral virtue ([Sahih Muslim 2721a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2721a)).
s13.narrative: Abdullah reported that Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) used to supplicate (in these words): "O Allah, I beg of Thee the right guidance, safeguard against evils, chastity and freedom from want (Allahumma inni as'alukal-huda wat-tuqa wal-'afafa wal-ghina)." — [Sahih Muslim 2721a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2721a)
benefits: **Comprehensive Spiritual & Moral Sufficiency:** Combines clarity of truth (*al-huda*), God-consciousness (*at-tuqa*), moral chastity and integrity (*al-'afaf*), and contentment of the heart free from needing people (*al-ghina*) ([Sahih Muslim 2721a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2721a)).

s14.heading: Total Harmony of Faith, Life & Hereafter: Making Life an Increase in Every Good and Death a Rest From Every Evil
s14.story: **Abu Hurairah (رضي الله عنه)** narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to supplicate with these five balanced petitions that set right a believer's religion, worldly livelihood, eternal destination, span of life, and moment of death ([Sahih Muslim 2720](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2720)).
s14.narrative: Abu Huraira reported that Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) used to supplicate (in these words): "O Allah, set right for me my religion which is the safeguard of my affairs. And set right for me the affairs of my world wherein is my living. And set right for me my Hereafter on which depends my after-life. And make the life for me (a source) of abundance for every good and make my death a source of comfort for me protecting me against every evil." — [Sahih Muslim 2720](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2720)
benefits: **Rectifies All Three Realms:** Sets right one's *Din* (the fortress of all affairs), one's *Dunya* (where one's livelihood resides), and one's *Akhirah* (one's eternal return), while turning every extra day of life into an increase in good deeds and making death a peaceful relief from every evil ([Sahih Muslim 2720](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2720)).

s15.heading: Dissolving Crushing Anguish (Du'a al-Karb): Proclaiming Allah's Majesty in the Darkest Hour
s15.story: **'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas (رضي الله عنهما)** transmitted the exact words that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would utter whenever a heavy crisis, anguish, or distress (*karb*) befell him—proclaiming the absolute Oneness and Sovereignty of the Lord of the Mighty Throne ([Sahih al-Bukhari 6346](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6346)).
s15.narrative: Narrated Ibn `Abbas: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) used to say at a time of distress, "La ilaha illal-lahu al-'Azimul-Halim, La ilaha illal-lahu Rabbul-'arshil-'azim, La ilaha illallahu Rabbus-samawati wa Rabbul-ard, wa Rabbul-'arshil-Karim (There is none worthy of worship but Allah, the Mighty, the Forbearing; there is none worthy of worship but Allah, Lord of the Magnificent Throne; there is none worthy of worship but Allah, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, and Lord of the Noble Throne)." — [Sahih al-Bukhari 6346](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6346)
benefits: **Relief from Severe Anguish (*Karb*):** Lifts heavy emotional and situational distress by exalting Allah's forbearance (*Al-Halim*) and supreme authority over the heavens, earth, and Throne ([Sahih al-Bukhari 6346](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6346)).

s16.heading: Deliverance From the Three Darknesses: The Call of Prophet Yunus (عليه السلام) That Is Always Answered
s16.story: Revealed in [Surah Al-Anbiya 21:87–88](https://quran.com/es/al-anbiya/87) where Allah rescued Prophet Yunus (Jonah, عليه السلام) from the belly of the whale and promised *"And thus do We save the believers,"* the Companion **Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (رضي الله عنه)** narrated that the Prophet ﷺ promised that *no* Muslim ever supplicates with this prayer concerning any matter whatsoever except that Allah answers him ([Jami` at-Tirmidhi 3505](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3505)).
s16.narrative: Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Sa`d narrated from his father, from Sa`d that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The supplication of Dhun-Nun (Prophet Yunus) when he supplicated, while in the belly of the whale was: 'There is none worthy of worship except You, Glory to You, Indeed, I have been of the transgressors (Lā ilāha illā anta subḥānaka innī kuntu minaẓ-ẓālimīn).' So indeed, no Muslim man supplicates with it for anything, ever, except Allah responds to him." — [Jami` at-Tirmidhi 3505](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3505)
benefits: **Guaranteed Acceptance of Supplication:** No Muslim calls upon Allah with these words regarding any need or distress except that Allah responds to them and rescues them from their anguish ([Jami` at-Tirmidhi 3505](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3505); [Surah Al-Anbiya 21:87–88](https://quran.com/es/al-anbiya/87)).

s17.heading: Lifting Grief & Crushing Debt: What the Prophet ﷺ Taught Abu Umamah Sitting Distressed in the Mosque
s17.story: **Anas ibn Malik (رضي الله عنه)** served the Prophet ﷺ and heard him recite this eightfold refuge constantly ([Sahih al-Bukhari 6369](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6369)). Furthermore, **Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (رضي الله عنه)** narrated a moving incident: one day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the mosque outside of prayer time and saw an Ansari Companion named **Abu Umamah (رضي الله عنه)** sitting alone, weighed down by sorrow. When the Prophet ﷺ asked why he was sitting in the mosque outside prayer hours, Abu Umamah replied: *"Worries and debts have surrounded me, O Messenger of Allah!"* The Prophet ﷺ taught him to say these exact eight refuges every morning and evening. Abu Umamah testified: *"I did that, and Allah removed my distress and settled my debt!"* ([Sunan Abi Dawud 1555](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:1555)).
s17.narrative:
Narrated Anas bin Malik: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to say, "O Allah! I seek refuge with You from worry and grief, from incapacity and laziness, from cowardice and miserliness, from being heavily in debt and from being overpowered by (other) men." — [Sahih al-Bukhari 6369](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6369)

Narrated AbuSa'id al-Khudri: One day the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered the mosque. He saw there a man from the Ansar called AbuUmamah. He said: "What is the matter that I am seeing you sitting in the mosque when there is no time of prayer?" He said: "I am entangled in cares and debts, Messenger of Allah." He replied: "Shall I not teach you words by which, when you say them, Allah will remove your care, and settle your debt?" He said: "Why not, Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Say in the morning and evening: 'O Allah, I seek refuge in Thee from care and grief, I seek refuge in Thee from incapacity and slackness, I seek refuge in Thee from cowardice and niggardliness, and I seek in Thee from being overcome by debt and being put in subjection by men.'" He said: "When I did that Allah removed my care and settled my debt." — [Sunan Abi Dawud 1555](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:1555)
benefits: **Relief from Anxiety (*Hamm*) & Sorrow (*Hazan*):** Heals both anxiety over the future (*hamm*) and grief over the past (*hazan*) ([Sahih al-Bukhari 6369](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6369)).

**Freedom from Crushing Debt & Oppression:** Protects against incapacity, laziness, cowardice, stinginess, the crushing weight of debt (*dala' ad-dayn*), and being overpowered or bullied by people (*ghalabat ar-rijal*) ([Sahih al-Bukhari 6369](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6369); [Sunan Abi Dawud 1555](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:1555)).

s18.heading: Preserving Allah's Blessings: Protection From the Loss of Favor, Failing Health & Sudden Calamity
s18.story: **'Abdullah ibn 'Umar (رضي الله عنهما)** preserved this profound supplication of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, which asks Allah to protect existing blessings from slipping away and to preserve one's state of well-being from suddenly turning into affliction ([Sahih Muslim 2739](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2739)).
s18.narrative: 'Abdullah b. Umar reported that Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) supplicated in these words: "O Allah, I seek refuge in Thee from the withdrawal of Thine blessing and the change of Thine protection (from me) and from the sudden wrath of Thine, and from every displeasure of Thine (Allahumma inni a'udhu bika min zawali ni'matika, wa tahawwuli 'afiyatika, wa fuja'ati niqmatika, wa jami'i sakhatika)." — [Sahih Muslim 2739](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2739)
benefits: **Safeguards Existing Blessings & Health:** Protects the believer against losing blessings they already enjoy (*zawali ni'matik*) and against health and security turning into sickness or trial (*tahawwuli 'afiyatik*) ([Sahih Muslim 2739](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2739)).

**Shields Against Sudden Retribution:** Protects against sudden, unexpected calamity and everything that incurs Allah's displeasure ([Sahih Muslim 2739](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2739)). ### Category 5: Debt and Provision (1 Dua)

s19.heading: The Shield of Ibrahim for Our Children: Protecting Little Ones From Devils, Pests & the Envious Eye
s19.story: **'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas (رضي الله عنهما)** narrated how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would lovingly place his grandsons **Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn (رضي الله عنهما)** under Allah's protection using the exact words with which Prophet Ibrahim (عليه السلام) used to seek refuge for his sons Isma'il and Ishaq (عليهما السلام) ([Sahih al-Bukhari 3371](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3371)).
s19.narrative: Narrated Ibn `Abbas: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to seek Refuge with Allah for Al-Hasan and Al-Husain and say: "Your forefather (i.e. Abraham) used to seek Refuge with Allah for Ishmael and Isaac by reciting the following: 'O Allah! I seek Refuge with Your Perfect Words from every devil and from poisonous pests and from every evil, harmful, envious eye (A'udhu bi-kalimatillahit-tammati min kulli shaytanin wa hammah, wa min kulli 'aynin lammah).'" — [Sahih al-Bukhari 3371](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3371)
benefits: **Threefold Shield for Children:** Protects children from every devil (*shaytan*), every venomous or harmful creature (*hammah*), and every struck, envious evil eye (*'aynin lammah*) ([Sahih al-Bukhari 3371](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3371)).

s20.heading: Self-Ruqyah for Physical Pain: How the Prophet ﷺ Relieved 'Uthman ibn Abi al-'As's Severe Bodily Ache
s20.story: This is one of the clearest examples of a Sahabi coming to the Prophet ﷺ in severe physical pain. **'Uthman ibn Abi al-'As ath-Thaqafi (رضي الله عنه)** came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ complaining of a debilitating pain in his body that had afflicted him ever since he embraced Islam and almost prevented him from praying. The Prophet ﷺ instructed him to place his own hand directly on the painful spot, say *Bismillah* 3 times, and recite this refuge 7 times. 'Uthman reported that he did so, and Allah completely removed his pain, and he continued teaching it to his family and others ([Sahih Muslim 2202](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2202)).
s20.narrative: Uthman b. Abu al-'As Al-Thaqafi reported that he made a complaint of pain to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) that he felt in his body at the time he had become Muslim. Thereupon Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: "Place your hand at the place where you feel pain in your body and say Bismillah (in the name of Allah) three times and seven times A'udhu billahi wa qudratihi min sharri ma ajidu wa uhadhiru (I seek refuge with Allah and with His Power from the evil that I find and that I fear)." — [Sahih Muslim 2202](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2202)
benefits: **Direct Relief of Physical Pain & Anxiety Over Illness:** Combines placing the hand on the painful area with seeking refuge in Allah's might from both the present pain (*ma ajidu*, what I feel now) and future fear of the illness worsening (*wa uhadhiru*, what I dread) ([Sahih Muslim 2202](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2202)). ### Category 4: Distress and Hardship (5 Duas)

s21.heading: Freedom From Indecision & Regret: How the Prophet ﷺ Taught Istikharah for Every Matter Great and Small
s21.story: **Jabir ibn 'Abdullah (رضي الله عنهما)** recalled with awe how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to teach the Companions to make *Istikharah* (seeking Allah's choice) in *all* their affairs, teaching them the exact words with the same care as he taught them a Surah from the Quran ([Sahih al-Bukhari 1166](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1166)).
s21.narrative: Narrated Jabir bin `Abdullah: The Prophet (p.b.u.h) used to teach us the way of doing Istikhara (Istikhara means to ask Allah to guide one to the right sort of action concerning any job or a deed), in all matters as he taught us the Suras of the Qur'an. He used to say, "If anyone of you thinks of doing any job he should offer a two Rakat prayer other than the compulsory ones and say (after the prayer): 'Allahumma inni astakhiruka bi'ilmika, Wa astaqdiruka bi-qudratika, Wa as'alaka min fadlika Al-`azim Fa-innaka taqdiru Wala aqdiru, Wa ta'lamu Wala a'lamu, Wa anta 'allamu l-ghuyub. Allahumma, in kunta ta'lam anna hadha-lamra Khairun li fi dini wa ma'ashi wa'aqibati `Amri (or 'ajili `Amri wa'ajilihi) Faqdirhu wa yas-sirhu li thumma barik li Fihi, Wa in kunta ta'lamu anna hadha-lamra shar-run li fi dini wa ma'ashi wa'aqibati `Amri (or fi'ajili `Amri wa ajilihi) Fasrifhu anni was-rifni anhu. Waqdir li al-khaira haithu kana Thumma ardini bihi.' (O Allah! I ask guidance from Your knowledge, And Power from Your Might and I ask for Your great blessings. You are capable and I am not. You know and I do not and You know the unseen. O Allah!
