If You know that this job is good for my religion and my subsistence and in my Hereafter — (or said: If it is better for my present and later needs) — Then You ordain it for me and make it easy for me to get, And then bless me in it, and if You know that this job is harmful to me in my religion and subsistence and in the Hereafter — (or said: If it is worse for my present and later needs) — Then keep it away from me and let me be away from it. And ordain for me whatever is good for me, And make me satisfied with it)." The Prophet (ﷺ) added that then the person should name (mention) his need. — [Sahih al-Bukhari 1166](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1166)
benefits: **Peace of Heart & Protection from Regret:** Entrusts the outcome of any decision to Allah's knowledge of the unseen—ensuring that if a path is good for one's faith and life, Allah facilitates and blesses it, and if harmful, Allah turns it away and grants contentment with whatever is best ([Sahih al-Bukhari 1166](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1166)).

s22.heading: The Fourfold Shield Before Taslim: Protection From the Grave, Hellfire, Life's Trials & Dajjal
s22.story: **Abu Hurairah (رضي الله عنه)** and **Ibn 'Abbas (رضي الله عنهما)** narrated that the Prophet ﷺ taught his Companions this fourfold refuge as meticulously as he taught them a Surah of the Quran, instructing them to recite it after finishing the final *Tashahhud* before giving the *Salam* ([Sahih al-Bukhari 1377](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1377); [Jami` at-Tirmidhi 3604](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3604)).
s22.narrative: Narrated Abu Huraira: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) used to invoke (Allah): "Allahumma inni a`udhu bika min 'adhabi-l-Qabr, wa min 'adhabi-nnar, wa min fitnati-l-mahya wa-lmamat, wa min fitnati-l-masih ad-dajjal. (O Allah! I seek refuge with you from the punishment in the grave and from the punishment in the Hell fire and from the afflictions of life and death, and the afflictions of Al-Masih Ad-Dajjal.)" — [Sahih al-Bukhari 1377](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1377)
benefits: **Protection from the Four Greatest Trials:** Shields the believer from the torment of the grave, the torment of Hell, the trials and temptations of life and the moment of death, and the supreme tribulation of the false messiah (*Al-Masih Ad-Dajjal*) ([Sahih al-Bukhari 1377](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1377)).

s23.heading: The Prayer of the Most Righteous: How the Prophet ﷺ Taught Abu Bakr as-Siddiq to Seek Forgiveness in Salah
s23.story: Even though **Abu Bakr as-Siddiq (رضي الله عنه)** was the most righteous of this Ummah after the Prophet ﷺ, he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked: *"O Messenger of Allah, teach me an invocation with which I may supplicate to Allah in my prayer."* The Prophet ﷺ taught him to confess having wronged himself greatly and to ask for forgiveness and mercy directly from Allah's presence ([Sahih al-Bukhari 834](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:834)).
s23.narrative: Narrated Abu Bakr As-Siddiq: I asked Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) to teach me an invocation so that I may invoke Allah with it in my prayer. He told me to say, "Allahumma inni zalamtu nafsi zulman kathiran, wala yaghfiru dh-dhunuba illa anta, faghfir li maghfiratan min `indika, war-hamni, innaka antal-ghafurur-rahim (O Allah! I have done great injustice to myself and none except You forgives sins, so bestow on me a forgiveness from You, and Have Mercy on me, You are the Forgiver, the Merciful)." — [Sahih al-Bukhari 834](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:834)
benefits: **Special Forgiveness & Mercy From Allah's Presence:** Draws down *maghfiratan min 'indika* (a special, unmerited forgiveness from Allah Himself) and divine mercy during the intimate standing of prayer ([Sahih al-Bukhari 834](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:834)). ### Category 3: Illness and Healing (4 Duas)

s24.heading: Wiping the Slate Clean on the Night of Decree: The Five Words Taught to 'Aishah (رضي الله عنها)
s24.story: The Mother of the Believers, **'Aishah (رضي الله عنها)**, asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ a question every believer wonders during the last ten nights of Ramadan: *"O Messenger of Allah, if I know which night is Laylatul-Qadr (the Night of Decree), what should I say during it?"* Out of all possible requests, he taught her to ask for *'Afw*—complete effacement and pardon of sins ([Jami` at-Tirmidhi 3513](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3513)).
s24.narrative: Aishah narrated: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what is your view if I know when the Night of Al-Qadr is, then what should I say in it?' He said: 'Say: "O Allah, indeed You are Pardoning, [Generous,] You love pardon, so pardon me (Allāhumma innaka `Afuwwun [Karīmun], tuḥibbul-`afwa fa`fu `annī)."'" — [Jami` at-Tirmidhi 3513](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3513)
benefits: **Complete Effacement of Sins (*'Afw*):** Invokes Allah by His Name *Al-'Afuww* (The One Who completely erases and wipes away every trace of sin) on a night better than a thousand months ([Jami` at-Tirmidhi 3513](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3513)). ### Category 11: Comprehensive Duas (3 Duas)

s25.heading: The Minor Death & Daily Resurrection: Entrusting Your Soul at Sleep and Thanking Allah Upon Waking
s25.story: The close confidant of the Prophet ﷺ, **Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman (رضي الله عنه)**, and **Abu Dharr (رضي الله عنه)** narrated how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entrusted his soul to Allah every night when laying his head down and praised Allah for restoring life every morning when opening his eyes ([Sahih al-Bukhari 6324](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6324)).
s25.narrative: Narrated Hudhaifa: Whenever the Prophet (ﷺ) intended to go to bed, he would recite: "Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya (With Your name, O Allah, I die and I live)." And when he woke up from his sleep, he would say: "Al-hamdu lil-lahil-ladhi ahyana ba'da ma amatana; wa ilaihi an-nushur (All the Praises are for Allah Who has made us alive after He made us die (sleep) and unto Him is the Resurrection)." — [Sahih al-Bukhari 6324](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6324)
benefits: **Peaceful Sleep & Grateful Awakening:** Closes the day in remembrance of Allah's name and opens the morning with gratitude for a new chance at life ([Sahih al-Bukhari 6324](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6324)).

s26.heading: "You Are Guided, Sufficed & Protected": The Step-Out-the-Door Dua That Makes Satan Turn Away
s26.story: **Anas ibn Malik (رضي الله عنه)** narrated a vivid unseen scene described by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: the moment a believer steps out of their home and utters these three phrases of trust in Allah, an angel proclaims that they are guided, sufficed, and protected, causing the devils to retreat in frustration ([Sunan Abi Dawud 5095](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5095)).
s26.narrative: Narrated Anas ibn Malik: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: When a man goes out of his house and says: "In the name of Allah, I trust in Allah; there is no might and no power but in Allah (Bismillahi, tawakkaltu 'alallahi, wa la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah)," the following will be said to him at that time: "You are guided, defended and protected." The devils will go far from him and another devil will say: "How can you deal with a man who has been guided, defended and protected?" — [Sunan Abi Dawud 5095](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5095)
benefits: **Threefold Angelic Guarantee:** The person is immediately told: *"You are guided (hudita), sufficed/defended (kufita), and protected (wuqita)"* ([Sunan Abi Dawud 5095](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5095)).

**Devils Cannot Harm or Mislead Them:** Shaytan steps aside, and one devil tells another that they have no power over someone who has been guided, sufficed, and protected ([Sunan Abi Dawud 5095](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5095)).

s27.heading: Stepping Into Mercy, Stepping Out Into Bounty: The Prophetic Words for Entering and Leaving the Masjid
s27.story: The Badr veteran **Abu Usayd al-Ansari (Malik ibn Rabi'ah, رضي الله عنه)** narrated the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ instruction to ask for the doors of Allah's Mercy (*Rahmah*) when entering the house of prayer, and to ask for Allah's Bounty/Provision (*Fadl*) when stepping back out into the world to earn a living ([Sahih Muslim 713a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:713a)).
s27.narrative: Abu Usaid reported that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When any one of you enters the mosque, he should say: 'O Allah! open for me the doors of Thy mercy (Allahummaf-tah li abwaba rahmatik)'; and when he steps out he should say: 'O Allah! I beg of Thee Thy Grace (Allahumma inni as'aluka min fadlik).'" — [Sahih Muslim 713a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:713a)
benefits: **Mercy Inside & Provision Outside:** Opens the doors of spiritual mercy inside the mosque and opens the doors of lawful bounty when stepping out into daily life ([Sahih Muslim 713a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:713a)).

s28.heading: The Traveler's Peace of Mind: Asking Allah to Fold the Distance & Guard the Family Left Behind
s28.story: **'Abdullah ibn 'Umar (رضي الله عنهما)** described how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, whenever he placed his foot in the stirrup and settled upon his camel to depart on a journey, would proclaim *Allahu Akbar* three times and recite this comprehensive travel supplication—and upon returning home, would add words of repentance and praise ([Sahih Muslim 1342](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1342)).
s28.narrative: Ibn Umar (Allah be pleased with them) reported that whenever Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) mounted his camel while setting out on a journey, he glorified Allah (uttered Allah-o-Akbar) thrice, and then said: "Hallowed is He Who subdued for us this (ride) and we were not ourselves powerful enough to use it as a ride, and we are going to return to our Lord. O Allah, we seek virtue and piety from Thee in this journey of ours and the act which pleaseth Thee. O Allah, lighten this journey of ours, and make its distance easy for us. O Allah, Thou art (our) companion during the journey, and guardian of (our) family. O Allah, I seek refuge with Thee from hardships of the journey, gloominess of the sights, and finding of evil changes in property and family on return." And he (the Holy Prophet) uttered (these words), and made this addition to them (upon returning): "We are returning, repentant, worshipping our Lord, and praising Him." — [Sahih Muslim 1342](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1342)
benefits: **Ease of Travel & Protection of Family:** Asks Allah to make the journey easy, fold its distance, accompany the traveler on the road, and act as the Guardian (*Khalifah*) over the family and property left behind ([Sahih Muslim 1342](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1342)). ### Category 10: Special Occasions (2 Duas)

s29.heading: The Seal of Forgiveness for Every Gathering: Erasing Idle Talk & Slips of the Tongue Before You Rise
s29.story: **Abu Hurairah (رضي الله عنه)** narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught his Companions how to expiate any idle chatter or unintentional slips of the tongue that occur when people sit together, simply by reciting these words before rising from the seat ([Jami` at-Tirmidhi 3433](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3433)).
s29.narrative: Abu Hurairah narrated that: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever sits in a sitting and engages in much empty, meaningless speech and then says before getting up from that sitting of his: 'Glory is to You, O Allah, and praise, I bear witness that there is none worthy of worship except You, I seek Your forgiveness, and I repent to You (Subḥānaka Allāhumma wa biḥamdika, ashhadu an lā ilāha illā anta, astaghfiruka wa atūbu ilaik),' whatever occurred in that sitting would be forgiven to him." — [Jami` at-Tirmidhi 3433](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3433)
benefits: **Complete Expiation of the Gathering:** Forgives whatever idle talk or minor shortcomings took place during that sitting ([Jami` at-Tirmidhi 3433](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3433)). ### Category 9: Daily Life (4 Duas)

s30.heading: Honoring Those Who Raised Us: Invoking Divine Mercy Upon Our Parents & All Believers
s30.story: Commanded directly by Allah in [Surah Al-Isra 17:24](https://quran.com/al-isra/24) as the ultimate expression of lowering the wing of humility to one's aging parents, and supplicated by Prophet Ibrahim (عليه السلام) in [Surah Ibrahim 14:41](https://quran.com/ibrahim/41-52) for himself, his parents, and all believers on the Day of Reckoning.
s30.narrative:
Quranic Verse (17:24): "And be humble with them out of mercy, and pray, 'My Lord! Be merciful to them as they raised me when I was young (Rabbir-hamhuma kama rabbayani saghira).'" — [Surah Al-Isra 17:24](https://quran.com/al-isra/24)

Quranic Verse (14:41): "Our Lord! Forgive me, my parents, and the believers on the Day when the judgment will come to pass (Rabbanagh-fir li wa li-walidayya wa lil-mu'minina yawma yaqumul-hisab)." — [Surah Ibrahim 14:41](https://quran.com/ibrahim/41-52)
benefits: **Mercy & Elevation for Parents:** Fulfills the Quranic command of *Birr al-Walidayn* (dutifulness to parents) during their life and after their passing, and includes all believers in forgiveness on the Day of Reckoning ([Surah Al-Isra 17:24](https://quran.com/al-isra/24); [Surah Ibrahim 14:41](https://quran.com/ibrahim/41-52)). ### Category 7: Guidance and Steadfastness (4 Duas)

s31.heading: Protection From Spiritual Relapse: The Prayer of the Firmly Grounded Against Deviation
s31.story: **'Aishah (رضي الله عنها)** narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited [Surah Ali 'Imran 3:7–8](https://quran.com/ali-imran/8) and warned the believers to beware of those who chase ambiguous matters to stir up dissension (*fitnah*), contrasting them with those firmly grounded in knowledge who pray: *"Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us"* ([Sahih al-Bukhari 4547](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4547); [Sahih Muslim 2665](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2665)).
s31.narrative: Narrated `Aisha: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) recited the Verse: "It is He who has sent down to you the Book. In it are Verses that are entirely clear, they are the foundation of the Book, others not entirely clear. So as for those in whose hearts there is a deviation (from the Truth), they follow thereof that is not entirely clear seeking affliction and searching for its hidden meanings; but no one knows its hidden meanings but Allah. And those who are firmly grounded in knowledge say: 'We believe in it (i.e. in the Qur'an) the whole of it (i.e. its clear and unclear Verses) are from our Lord. And none receive admonition except men of understanding.' (3:7)" Then Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "If you see those who follow thereof that is not entirely clear, then they are those whom Allah has named [as having deviation (from the Truth)] 'So beware of them.'" — [Sahih al-Bukhari 4547](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4547)
benefits: **Safeguard Against Deviation After Guidance:** Protects the believer from losing faith or straying into doubt after Allah has blessed them with guidance, and draws down mercy directly from *Al-Wahhab* (The Bestower) ([Surah Ali 'Imran 3:8](https://quran.com/ali-imran/8); [Sahih al-Bukhari 4547](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4547)). ### Category 8: Gatherings (2 Duas)
